The sweep is missing likely core intervention types such as teacher professional-development programs on formative assessment, digital adaptive assessment systems, classroom feedback interventions, and studies with delayed posttests or retention/transfer measures.
There is little or no coverage of implementation tradeoffs reported by teachers/schools (time burden, feasibility, uptake, fidelity, training intensity, adaptation), which are central to the thread.
The current findings seem weighted toward early math and a single recent paper; broader K-12 and multiple implementation contexts are not yet adequately represented.

The sweep has only surfaced one likely relevant meta-analysis on formative assessment in reading, but no extracted subgroup/moderator estimates for the target populations (English language learners, students with disabilities, low-income students) or prior-achievement strata.
The evidence currently appears to be about generic moderators (sample size, grade level, intervention type, etc.) rather than equity-relevant subgroups specifically named in the research thread.
No direct formative-assessment intervention studies with subgroup or moderator effects have been identified yet.

No review excerpts or meta-analytic results have been captured that explicitly report quantitative estimates for ELL, disability, socioeconomic status/low-income, or prior achievement groups; only narrative mention of 'student characteristics' appears so far.
The current finding is incomplete because it does not yet distinguish between extractable quantitative subgroup results and merely narrative suggestions in the source literature.
No direct formative-assessment intervention studies are identified yet; the sweep is heavily weighted toward protocols, unrelated meta-analyses, and general edtech reviews.

No extractable subgroup/moderator quantitative estimates are reported for the target populations (English language learners, students with disabilities, low-income students, prior achievement strata).
The current set does not surface review excerpts or meta-analyses that explicitly discuss subgroup effects in K-12 formative assessment, nor narrative-only moderator mentions.
Several potentially relevant items are only abstracts/paywalled, limiting ability to verify whether subgroup analyses exist.

Coverage is too narrow: only one clear K-12 formative-assessment meta-analysis is surfaced, focused on reading achievement, so the sweep does not yet cover broader formative-assessment interventions across subjects or grade bands.

Implementation features central to the thread are undercovered: there is little evidence retrieved on feedback quality, implementation fidelity, teacher training/professional development, dosage/duration, digital tools, feasibility/workload, or delayed posttests/retention/transfer.

No distinct intervention studies are yet identified that let you extract implementation tradeoffs alongside student-achievement links; the current result is a review-level finding rather than a set of primary studies and implementation-focused syntheses.
The search appears constrained by Semantic Scholar 403 errors, so likely misses important review articles and RCTs in databases/indexes not reachable via the current query path.
Only one meta-analysis on reading achievement is shown so far; the sweep is missing broader K-12 formative-assessment interventions across subjects and age bands.
The current evidence emphasizes differentiated instruction, but there is little/no coverage of implementation tradeoffs such as teacher workload, feasibility, fidelity, or training dose/duration.
No clear coverage of digital or computer-based formative-assessment tools, despite the thread explicitly asking for implementation features and tradeoffs.
Delayed posttests, retention, and transfer outcomes are not surfaced in the findings so far.

There is no evident set of primary intervention studies with extractable links to student achievement; the sweep appears review-heavy and may be missing classroom trials/RCTs and design-based studies.
Assessment quality dimensions like feedback specificity/timeliness and how feedback was generated are not yet well covered.
